Raw_Description: Footage from Lord & Taylor shows two young men carrying heavy backpacks near the finish line moments before detonations. Suspects appear to act alone.
Crime scene sweep recovers fragments of a pressure cooker, nails, ball bearings, and black powder. Components are readily available domestically.
Analysis of recovered computer search history shows queries for 'Inspire magazine', 'how to build bombs', and radical jihadist literature.
Bank records indicate a recent wire transfer of $1,200 to an account in Dagestan, Russia.
Suspects' social media profiles show anti-American sentiment but no direct communication with known foreign terrorist networks.
Firearms recovered from Watertown shootout are unregistered and traced back to local private sales, not international arms dealers.
Informant suggests suspects may have received explosive training during a 2012 trip to Russia.
Initial statements from surviving suspect indicate they acted independently to defend Islam, using internet instructions, with no outside command.
